questions.subdomain: Manage Microsoft Entra users and groups
questions.question: An administrator must create 300 user accounts in Microsoft Entra ID from a list in a spreadsheet. What is the most efficient method?
options: Use the bulk create operation with a CSV template, or a PowerShell script with Microsoft Graph
Create each user one at a time in the portal
Ask each user to create their own account
Create one shared account for all 300 users
questions.correct_rationale: Bulk create and scripting add many users quickly and consistently.
questions.distractor_summary: Manual creation is slow, self-creation is not how tenant accounts work, and shared accounts break accountability.

questions.subdomain: Manage Microsoft Entra users and groups
questions.question: Users in the Sales department should be added to a group automatically based on the department attribute in their profiles. What should be configured?
options: An assigned membership group updated by hand
A Microsoft 365 group with no members
A resource lock on the group
A dynamic membership group with a rule on the department attribute
questions.correct_rationale: Dynamic groups add and remove members automatically based on user attributes.
questions.distractor_summary: Assigned groups need manual updates, an empty group does nothing, and locks do not manage membership.

questions.subdomain: Manage Microsoft Entra users and groups
questions.question: Which license is required to use dynamic membership groups in Microsoft Entra ID?
options: No license, as it is included in the Free tier
Microsoft Entra ID P1 or higher
questions.correct_rationale: Dynamic groups need at least Entra ID P1 licensing for the members they affect.
questions.distractor_summary: The Free tier does not include dynamic groups, and DevOps or Visual Studio licenses do not grant the feature.

questions.subdomain: Manage Microsoft Entra users and groups
questions.question: An administrator wants to give a group of users a license for a Microsoft service and have new group members receive it automatically. What should be used?
options: Assigning licenses to each user by hand
Group-based licensing in Microsoft Entra ID
questions.correct_rationale: Group-based licensing assigns licenses to all members and updates them as membership changes.
questions.distractor_summary: Manual assignment does not scale, and Policy and budgets do not assign licenses.

questions.subdomain: Manage Microsoft Entra users and groups
questions.question: What is a guest user in Microsoft Entra ID?
options: A user who can sign in without any password or method
An external user invited through B2B collaboration who signs in with their own identity
A service principal for an application
questions.correct_rationale: Guest users come from outside the organization and are invited to access resources.
questions.distractor_summary: Guests still authenticate, service principals represent apps, and guest is not an admin role.

questions.subdomain: Manage Microsoft Entra users and groups
questions.question: Users must be able to reset their own passwords without calling the help desk. What should be enabled?
options: A resource lock on the user objects
questions.correct_rationale: SSPR lets users reset passwords after verifying with registered methods.
questions.distractor_summary: Blocking access, locks, and Azure Policy do not provide password reset.

questions.subdomain: Manage Microsoft Entra users and groups
questions.question: A company wants self-service password reset to write changed passwords back to on-premises Active Directory. What must be configured?
options: A dynamic group for all users
Password writeback through Microsoft Entra Connect or Cloud Sync
questions.correct_rationale: Password writeback sends cloud password changes to on-premises AD.
questions.distractor_summary: A VPN alone does not write passwords back, and Azure Files and dynamic groups are unrelated.

questions.subdomain: Manage Microsoft Entra users and groups
questions.question: Which object represents an application's identity in a Microsoft Entra tenant so it can be granted access to resources?
questions.correct_rationale: Service principals are the tenant-local identities of applications.
questions.distractor_summary: Guests are people, dynamic groups hold members, and administrative units scope administration.

questions.subdomain: Manage Microsoft Entra users and groups
questions.question: Help desk staff in one region should reset passwords only for users in that region. What should be used?
options: The Global Administrator role for help desk staff
A management group for the region
An administrative unit containing those users, with the help desk role scoped to it
A resource group for the region
questions.correct_rationale: Administrative units restrict the scope of Entra directory roles to a subset of users.
questions.distractor_summary: Global Administrator is far too broad, and management and resource groups scope Azure resources rather than directory objects.

questions.subdomain: Manage Microsoft Entra users and groups
questions.question: Which group type can be used to assign permissions to Azure resources?
options: Dynamic device groups only for email
questions.correct_rationale: Security groups are used to assign access to resources, including Azure RBAC roles.
questions.distractor_summary: Distribution lists and contacts are for email, and device groups for email are not a real access mechanism.

questions.subdomain: Manage Microsoft Entra users and groups
questions.question: A user was deleted by mistake from Microsoft Entra ID yesterday. How can it be restored with its memberships intact?
options: Restore the user from Deleted users, which keeps deleted users for 30 days
Recreate the user with the same name
Restore it from an Azure Backup vault
Contact Microsoft to rebuild the tenant
questions.correct_rationale: Deleted users stay in a soft-deleted state for 30 days and can be restored with their attributes.
questions.distractor_summary: A new account gets a new object ID, Azure Backup does not back up Entra users, and rebuilding the tenant is unnecessary.

questions.subdomain: Manage Microsoft Entra users and groups
questions.question: External partners must sign in to your resources with their own Microsoft Entra accounts, and you want to review their access every quarter. What should be used?
options: A storage account SAS token for each partner
B2B guest users with Microsoft Entra access reviews
questions.correct_rationale: Access reviews let owners confirm or remove guest access on a schedule.
questions.distractor_summary: Shared accounts and broad admin rights are insecure, and SAS tokens grant storage access only.

questions.subdomain: Manage Microsoft Entra users and groups
questions.question: What does the Microsoft Entra ID device join feature allow?
options: Virtual machines to join an Azure virtual network
Storage accounts to join a resource group
Subscriptions to join a management group
Organization-owned Windows devices to join Entra ID so users sign in with their work accounts and devices can be managed
questions.correct_rationale: Entra join registers devices with the directory for sign-in and management.
questions.distractor_summary: The other choices describe networking or resource organization, not device identity.

questions.question: Which built-in Azure role can manage all resources but cannot grant access to others?
questions.correct_rationale: Contributor can create and manage resources but cannot assign roles.
questions.distractor_summary: Owner can assign roles, Reader is read-only, and User Access Administrator manages access only.

questions.question: Which built-in role lets a user manage access to Azure resources without managing the resources themselves?
questions.correct_rationale: User Access Administrator manages role assignments.
questions.distractor_summary: Contributor manages resources, Reader views, and Virtual Machine Contributor manages VMs.

questions.question: A user needs to view all resources in a subscription but must not change anything. Which role should be assigned, and at which scope?
options: Owner at a resource group scope
questions.correct_rationale: Reader at the subscription gives read access to everything in it.
questions.distractor_summary: Contributor and Owner grant changes, and one resource is too narrow.

questions.question: No built-in role allows exactly the actions a team needs: start, stop, and restart VMs only. What should the administrator do?
options: Create a custom role with only those actions and assign it at the needed scope
Assign Virtual Machine Contributor, which includes deleting VMs
Assign Owner and trust the team
Create a resource lock on the VMs
questions.correct_rationale: Custom roles define precise action lists for least privilege.
questions.distractor_summary: Broader roles grant extra rights, and locks do not grant permissions.

questions.question: In a custom role definition, what does the NotActions property do?
options: It denies those actions even if another role allows them
It lists the scopes where the role can be assigned
It removes specific actions from the set allowed by Actions
questions.correct_rationale: NotActions subtracts from Actions within the same role, but it is not an explicit deny.
questions.distractor_summary: Deny assignments are separate, DataActions list data operations, and AssignableScopes set scopes.

questions.question: Which tool shows the effective role assignments a specific user has on a resource group?
options: The Check access feature in Access control (IAM)
questions.correct_rationale: Check access lists the roles a user has at a scope, including inherited ones.
questions.distractor_summary: Advisor, Service Health, and the calculator do not show permissions.

questions.question: A role is assigned to a user at the management group level. The user also has Reader on one resource group. What permissions apply on that resource group?
options: Only Reader, because the closer assignment wins
The union of both: management group permissions are inherited, and Reader is added
Only the management group role, because higher scopes override lower ones
questions.correct_rationale: Azure RBAC is additive, so effective permissions combine all assignments.
questions.distractor_summary: Closer scopes do not override, assignments do not cancel, and higher scopes do not replace lower ones.

questions.question: Which Azure RBAC role allows reading blob data in a storage account?
questions.correct_rationale: Data plane access to blobs needs a data role such as Storage Blob Data Reader.
questions.distractor_summary: Reader and Storage Account Contributor are control plane roles, and VM Contributor is unrelated.

questions.question: An app running on an Azure VM must access a storage account without stored credentials. What should be used?
options: A managed identity for the VM with an RBAC role on the storage account
Storage account keys in the app's configuration file
questions.correct_rationale: Managed identities let Azure resources authenticate to services without secrets in code.
questions.distractor_summary: Stored keys and shared passwords are risky, and guest accounts are for people.

questions.question: What is the difference between a system-assigned and a user-assigned managed identity?
options: A user-assigned identity is deleted with the resource
A system-assigned identity can be shared by many resources
A system-assigned identity is tied to one resource's lifecycle, while a user-assigned identity is a separate resource that can be shared by several resources
questions.correct_rationale: User-assigned identities exist independently and can be attached to multiple resources.
questions.distractor_summary: They differ, and the deletion and sharing behaviors are reversed in the other choices.

questions.question: Resources in a subscription must only be created in East US and West US. What should be configured?
options: A resource lock on the subscription
A management group with no policies
An Azure Policy assignment using the Allowed locations definition
questions.correct_rationale: The Allowed locations policy denies deployments outside approved regions.
questions.distractor_summary: Locks prevent changes or deletion, and empty groups and Reader do not restrict locations.

questions.question: A production resource group must not be deleted accidentally, but its resources must still be updatable. What should be applied?
options: A ReadOnly lock on the resource group
A Deny policy for all resource types
A CanNotDelete lock on the resource group
The Reader role for all administrators
questions.correct_rationale: CanNotDelete prevents deletion while allowing changes.
questions.distractor_summary: ReadOnly blocks updates, a broad Deny policy blocks deployments, and Reader blocks all changes.

questions.question: Which statement about resource locks is correct?
options: Locks apply to all users and roles, and locks on a parent scope are inherited by child resources
Locks only apply to the resource where they are created
Locks can be applied only to storage accounts
questions.correct_rationale: Locks override permissions for everyone and are inherited downward.
questions.distractor_summary: Owners are not exempt, locks are inherited, and they apply to many resource types.

questions.question: A ReadOnly lock is placed on a storage account. Users report they can no longer list the account keys. Why?
options: Listing keys is a POST operation, which ReadOnly locks block
ReadOnly locks delete the account keys
ReadOnly locks disable the storage account
The lock removed the users' role assignments
questions.correct_rationale: ReadOnly blocks write and POST operations on the control plane, including listing keys.
questions.distractor_summary: Locks do not delete keys, disable accounts, or remove role assignments.

questions.question: What happens to tags on a resource group by default?
options: All resources inherit the tags automatically
Tags are copied to all subscriptions
Resources in the group do not inherit the tags automatically
questions.correct_rationale: Tags are not inherited by default, but Azure Policy can add or inherit them.
questions.distractor_summary: Automatic inheritance does not happen, tags do not spread to subscriptions, and they do not expire.

questions.question: Every resource must have a CostCenter tag copied from its resource group. What should be used?
options: A ReadOnly lock on all resources
The built-in Azure Policy that inherits a tag from the resource group, with a remediation task for existing resources
questions.correct_rationale: Policy with the Modify effect can inherit tags and fix existing resources.
questions.distractor_summary: Locks, spreadsheets, and roles do not apply tags automatically.

questions.question: A company wants to move a virtual machine and its disks to a different resource group in another subscription. What should be checked first?
options: That the VM is in the archive tier
That the subscription has no budgets
That the resource types support the move, that dependent resources move together, and that the destination subscription is in the same tenant with providers registered
That the VM has no tags
questions.correct_rationale: Moves require supported resource types, related resources, the same tenant, and registered resource providers.
questions.distractor_summary: Archive tiers, budgets, and tags do not block moves.

questions.question: Which Cost Management feature sends notifications when spending exceeds a threshold?
questions.correct_rationale: Budgets trigger alerts at percentages of a set amount.
questions.distractor_summary: Locks, initiatives, and management groups do not watch spending.

questions.question: An organization needs to apply the same policies and RBAC roles to 12 subscriptions for its production environment. What is the best design?
options: Place the subscriptions in a production management group and assign policies and roles there
Assign them separately in each subscription
Merge the subscriptions into one resource group
Use one tag on all subscriptions
questions.correct_rationale: Management groups apply governance across many subscriptions through inheritance.
questions.distractor_summary: Separate assignments drift, subscriptions cannot be merged into a resource group, and tags do not apply policies.

questions.question: Which Azure Policy effect adds, updates, or removes properties or tags on resources during creation or update?
questions.correct_rationale: Modify changes resource properties such as tags.
questions.distractor_summary: Audit reports, Deny blocks, and Disabled turns off evaluation.

questions.question: A policy is assigned with the DeployIfNotExists effect, but existing resources remain noncompliant. What is needed?
options: Deleting the policy and recreating it daily
Adding a CanNotDelete lock to the resources
A remediation task, run with the policy assignment's managed identity that has the required permissions
questions.correct_rationale: DeployIfNotExists fixes new deployments automatically, while existing resources need a remediation task.
questions.distractor_summary: Recreating policies does not remediate, locks block changes, and Audit only reports.

questions.question: A subscription owner wants to see why costs went up last month by service and resource group. What should they use?
options: Cost analysis in Microsoft Cost Management
questions.correct_rationale: Cost analysis breaks down actual spending by service, resource group, and tags.
questions.distractor_summary: Metric alerts track performance, Resource Graph lists resources, and the calculator estimates.

questions.question: Which tool provides fast queries across all resources in many subscriptions using a Kusto-based language?
questions.correct_rationale: Resource Graph queries resource properties at scale across subscriptions.
questions.distractor_summary: Storage Explorer browses data, Data Box moves data, and Network Watcher diagnoses networks.

questions.question: Administrators want to ensure no one can create public IP addresses in development subscriptions. What should be used?
options: An Azure Policy that denies the public IP address resource type
A Reader role for all developers
questions.correct_rationale: A deny policy for that resource type blocks creation.
questions.distractor_summary: Locks prevent deletion, Reader blocks all changes, and budgets only alert.

questions.question: What is required before you can create a resource type in a subscription for the first time?
options: The resource provider for that type must be registered in the subscription
A management group must be deleted
A support plan must be purchased
questions.correct_rationale: Resource providers must be registered, which often happens automatically on first use.
questions.distractor_summary: Deleting groups, buying support, and creating budgets are not prerequisites.

questions.question: A policy assignment should apply to a management group except for one sandbox subscription. How can this be done?
options: Move the policy to every other subscription manually
Apply a ReadOnly lock to the sandbox subscription
Add the sandbox subscription as an exclusion on the policy assignment, or use a policy exemption
questions.correct_rationale: Assignments support excluded scopes, and exemptions can waive specific resources or scopes.
questions.distractor_summary: Deleting or locking the subscription is drastic, and manual assignments drift.

questions.question: Which built-in role can manage Azure Policy assignments without managing other resources?
questions.correct_rationale: Resource Policy Contributor manages policy definitions and assignments.
questions.distractor_summary: The other roles cover data, VMs, or read access.

questions.question: A team wants to tag resources by environment and use those tags to filter costs. Which statement is correct?
options: Tags cannot be used in cost reports
Tags change the price of resources
Tags appear in cost data and can be used to group and filter in Cost Management
Tags are visible only to the Owner role
questions.correct_rationale: Cost Management uses tags to group and filter spending.
questions.distractor_summary: Tags can be used in reports, do not change prices, and are visible to anyone with read access.

questions.question: What is the maximum depth of the management group hierarchy, excluding the root and the subscription level?
questions.correct_rationale: Management group trees can be up to six levels deep under the root.
questions.distractor_summary: The depth is limited, but to six rather than one or two.

questions.question: A company must stop users from creating virtual machines with unmanaged disks. Which approach is best?
options: Assign the built-in policy that audits or denies VMs that do not use managed disks
Lock every resource group as ReadOnly
Remove the Contributor role from all users
Use a budget with a low limit
questions.correct_rationale: Built-in policies can target VM disk configuration directly.
questions.distractor_summary: Broad locks and role removal block all work, and budgets do not inspect disk types.

questions.question: Which scope is the highest at which you can assign Azure RBAC roles and policies?
questions.correct_rationale: The root management group sits above all management groups and subscriptions.
questions.distractor_summary: Resource groups, resources, and virtual networks are lower scopes.

questions.question: Which feature should a company use to make sure that only approved VM sizes can be deployed?
options: Azure Policy with the Allowed virtual machine size SKUs definition
questions.correct_rationale: This built-in policy restricts allowed VM sizes.
questions.distractor_summary: Advisor recommends, vaults back up, and NSGs filter traffic.

questions.question: A partner needs read access to one blob for 24 hours without any Azure account. What should be provided?
options: The Owner role on the storage account
A shared access signature with read permission and a 24-hour expiry
A public container with anonymous access forever
questions.correct_rationale: A SAS grants limited, time-bound access to specific resources.
questions.distractor_summary: Account keys give full access, Owner grants control of the account, and permanent public access is too broad.

questions.question: Which type of shared access signature is secured with Microsoft Entra credentials rather than the account key?
options: A service SAS signed with the account key
questions.correct_rationale: A user delegation SAS is signed with a key obtained using Entra credentials and is recommended for blobs.
questions.distractor_summary: Service and account SAS use the account key, and stored access policies are not SAS types.

questions.question: Several SAS tokens were issued for a container, and one must be revoked before its expiry without rotating the account key. What should have been used?
options: A stored access policy on the container that the SAS tokens reference, which can be changed or deleted to revoke them
An account SAS with no expiry
questions.correct_rationale: SAS tokens tied to a stored access policy can be revoked by changing the policy.
questions.distractor_summary: Account SAS without expiry is risky, locks do not revoke tokens, and Azure Files access is unrelated.

questions.question: Storage account keys may have been exposed. What should the administrator do?
options: Rotate the keys, regenerating one at a time while applications switch to the other key
questions.correct_rationale: Key rotation invalidates the old key, and the two keys allow rotation without downtime.
questions.distractor_summary: Deleting the account loses data, locks do not change keys, and tiers are unrelated.

questions.question: How can a storage account be restricted so that only specific virtual networks and IP ranges can reach it?
options: Configure the storage firewall and virtual networks settings, with selected networks only
questions.correct_rationale: Storage firewall rules limit network access to allowed subnets and IP addresses.
questions.distractor_summary: Roles control permissions, lifecycle rules move data, and soft delete protects against deletion.

questions.question: A VM in a subnet must reach a storage account over the Microsoft backbone, while public internet access to the account is blocked. Which feature uses a private IP address in the virtual network?
options: A service endpoint, which gives the account a private IP
A public IP on the storage account
A private endpoint for the storage account
questions.correct_rationale: Private endpoints create a network interface with a private IP for the storage account.
questions.distractor_summary: Service endpoints keep the public endpoint but restrict sources, storage accounts do not take public IPs, and NAT gateways handle outbound traffic.

questions.question: What does disabling shared key authorization on a storage account do?
options: It deletes all data in the account
It forces requests to use Microsoft Entra ID authorization instead of account keys or key-signed SAS
questions.correct_rationale: Disallowing shared key access requires Entra-based authorization for data requests.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not delete data, make containers public, or disable encryption.

questions.question: Users must access an Azure file share using their on-premises AD credentials with NTFS permissions. What should be configured?
options: A SAS token for each user
Identity-based authentication for Azure Files with AD DS or Microsoft Entra Domain Services, plus share-level RBAC
questions.correct_rationale: Azure Files supports identity-based SMB access with share and file-level permissions.
questions.distractor_summary: SAS tokens and anonymous access do not use AD identity, and vaults handle backup.

questions.question: Which setting should be disabled to prevent anyone from making blob containers publicly readable?
options: Allow Blob anonymous access at the storage account level
questions.correct_rationale: Turning off anonymous access stops containers from being made public.
questions.distractor_summary: Soft delete, versioning, and hierarchical namespace do not control public access.

questions.question: A company needs to encrypt storage data with keys it controls and can rotate. What should be configured?
options: An access tier change to archive
Customer-managed keys stored in Azure Key Vault, linked to the storage account
questions.correct_rationale: Customer-managed keys in Key Vault give the company control over the encryption keys.
questions.distractor_summary: Microsoft-managed keys are controlled by Microsoft, and locks and tiers do not change encryption keys.

questions.question: A storage account must keep data available if a single availability zone fails, and the data must stay in one region. Which redundancy fits?
questions.correct_rationale: ZRS keeps three copies across zones within one region.
questions.distractor_summary: LRS is one data center, and GRS options copy data to another region.

questions.question: Which storage account type supports premium performance for block blobs with low latency?
options: Standard general-purpose v2 with the cool tier
questions.correct_rationale: Premium block blob accounts use SSDs for low-latency blob workloads.
questions.distractor_summary: Standard and classic accounts do not offer premium blob performance.

questions.question: Data must be copied asynchronously from a storage account in one region to another for disaster recovery, and the company wants to fail over itself when needed. What should be configured?
options: Locally redundant storage with soft delete
Geo-redundant storage with customer-managed account failover
A lifecycle policy moving data to archive
questions.correct_rationale: GRS replicates to a secondary region, and customer-managed failover makes the secondary primary.
questions.distractor_summary: LRS and ZRS stay in one region, and lifecycle rules do not replicate data.

questions.question: Which tool can copy large amounts of data between storage accounts from the command line, with resume support?
questions.correct_rationale: AzCopy is designed for high-performance copying to and from storage.
questions.distractor_summary: The other tools do not copy data.

questions.question: Blobs in a container must be copied automatically to a storage account in another region as they are written. What should be configured?
options: Object replication between the source and destination containers, with versioning and change feed enabled as required
questions.correct_rationale: Object replication asynchronously copies block blobs between accounts.
questions.distractor_summary: Lifecycle rules change tiers, stored access policies control SAS, and File Sync works with file shares.

questions.question: What does enabling hierarchical namespace on a storage account provide?
options: Azure Data Lake Storage capabilities with directories and file-level access control lists
questions.correct_rationale: Hierarchical namespace turns Blob storage into Data Lake Storage with real directories and ACLs.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not affect DNS, replication, or encryption keys.

questions.question: Users must view and manage blobs, files, and queues in several storage accounts from a desktop application. What should they use?
questions.correct_rationale: Storage Explorer provides a graphical way to manage storage data.
questions.distractor_summary: Data Box is a shipping device, workbooks display monitoring, and Migrate moves workloads.

questions.subdomain: Configure Azure Files and Azure Blob Storage
questions.question: Deleted blobs must be recoverable for 14 days. What should be enabled?
options: A CanNotDelete lock on the storage account
Blob soft delete with a 14-day retention period
questions.correct_rationale: Soft delete keeps deleted blobs for the retention period so they can be restored.
questions.distractor_summary: Account locks do not protect individual blobs, archive is a tier, and stored access policies control SAS.

questions.subdomain: Configure Azure Files and Azure Blob Storage
questions.question: What does blob versioning do?
options: It keeps previous versions of a blob automatically when the blob is changed or deleted
It renames blobs with a version number
It moves blobs to another region
It encrypts blobs with a new key each time
questions.correct_rationale: Versioning saves earlier versions so they can be restored.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not rename, replicate, or re-encrypt blobs.

questions.subdomain: Configure Azure Files and Azure Blob Storage
questions.question: Compliance requires that certain blobs cannot be modified or deleted for seven years. What should be configured?
options: An immutable storage policy with time-based retention on the container or blob versions
A CanNotDelete lock on the resource group
questions.correct_rationale: Immutable storage with time-based retention enforces write-once, read-many protection.
questions.distractor_summary: Soft delete allows changes, locks protect the account but not blob contents, and archive is a cost tier.

questions.subdomain: Configure Azure Files and Azure Blob Storage
questions.question: Blobs that have not been modified for 30 days should move to the cool tier and be deleted after 365 days. What should be used?
questions.correct_rationale: Lifecycle rules change tiers and delete blobs based on age conditions.
questions.distractor_summary: Object replication copies data, stored access policies control SAS, and File Sync syncs shares.

questions.subdomain: Configure Azure Files and Azure Blob Storage
questions.question: What must happen before a blob in the archive tier can be read?
options: Nothing, because archive blobs can be read instantly
It must be copied to Azure Files
It must be rehydrated to the hot, cool, or cold tier, which can take hours
The storage account must be converted to premium
questions.correct_rationale: Archived blobs are offline and need rehydration before reading.
questions.distractor_summary: Archive data is not instantly readable, and Azure Files or premium conversion are not required.

questions.subdomain: Configure Azure Files and Azure Blob Storage
questions.question: Users on premises need fast local access to a file share that also lives in Azure, with rarely used files kept only in the cloud. What should be deployed?
options: Azure File Sync with cloud tiering on a Windows Server
questions.correct_rationale: File Sync caches frequently used files locally and tiers cold files to Azure.
questions.distractor_summary: AzCopy copies without caching, object replication is for blobs, and SAS controls access.

questions.subdomain: Configure Azure Files and Azure Blob Storage
questions.question: Which Azure Files feature lets users restore previous versions of files from a point-in-time copy?
questions.correct_rationale: Share snapshots capture read-only copies of a share that can be used for restore.
questions.distractor_summary: Versioning, lifecycle rules, and object replication apply to blobs.

questions.subdomain: Configure Azure Files and Azure Blob Storage
questions.question: A file share is deleted by mistake. How can it be recovered?
options: Enable soft delete for file shares beforehand, then undelete the share within the retention period
Use object replication to bring it back
Recreate it with the same name to restore the data
questions.correct_rationale: File share soft delete keeps deleted shares for a retention period.
questions.distractor_summary: Blob versioning and object replication do not cover file shares, and recreating the name does not restore data.

questions.subdomain: Configure Azure Files and Azure Blob Storage
questions.question: Which protocols can Azure file shares support?
options: SMB, and NFS on premium file shares
questions.correct_rationale: Azure Files supports SMB, plus NFS for premium shares, along with REST access.
questions.distractor_summary: FTP, iSCSI, and HTTP-only block storage do not describe Azure Files.

questions.subdomain: Configure Azure Files and Azure Blob Storage
questions.question: A team wants to copy files to Azure Files using a graphical tool, with drag-and-drop support. What fits?
questions.correct_rationale: Storage Explorer supports uploading files and folders to file shares.
questions.distractor_summary: Policy, Advisor, and Bastion do not transfer files.

questions.subdomain: Configure Azure Files and Azure Blob Storage
questions.question: What is the cold access tier for blobs?
options: An offline tier that needs rehydration
An online tier for data accessed rarely and kept at least 90 days, cheaper to store than cool but more expensive to access
A tier only for Azure Files
questions.correct_rationale: The cold tier sits between cool and archive and stays online.
questions.distractor_summary: It is not offline, premium, or limited to Azure Files.

questions.subdomain: Manage Microsoft Entra users and groups
questions.question: An administrator must invite 50 partner users as guests at once. What is the most efficient method?
options: Invite each user by hand in the portal
Use the bulk invite feature with a CSV file, or a script with Microsoft Graph
Create internal member accounts for each partner
Share one guest account among all partners
questions.correct_rationale: Bulk invite sends B2B invitations to many users from one file.
questions.distractor_summary: Manual invitations are slow, internal accounts misrepresent partners, and shared accounts break accountability.

questions.subdomain: Manage Microsoft Entra users and groups
questions.question: Which user property is used to decide whether a user is a member or a guest in Microsoft Entra ID?
questions.correct_rationale: The user type property is Member or Guest.
questions.distractor_summary: Usage location, job title, and department describe other attributes.

questions.question: An administrator needs to grant a contractor Contributor access to a resource group for only two weeks. What is the best approach?
options: Assign Contributor permanently and set a calendar reminder
Give the contractor the storage account keys
Use Privileged Identity Management to create a time-bound eligible or active assignment
questions.correct_rationale: PIM supports assignments with start and end dates and can require activation.
questions.distractor_summary: Reminders are unreliable, Owner is too broad, and keys are unrelated to the role.

questions.question: What does an Azure Policy definition's effect of Audit do?

questions.question: An administrator wants to make sure that clients connecting to a storage account use at least TLS 1.2. What should be configured?

questions.question: An existing storage account uses LRS, and the company now needs protection from a regional outage. What should be done?

questions.question: Which encryption is applied to data in Azure Storage by default?

Encryption only for the archive tier
Encryption only when using SAS tokens
Storage service encryption with 256-bit AES and Microsoft-managed keys

questions.question: An administrator must make sure that data written to a storage account is also encrypted with a second layer of encryption at the infrastructure level. What should be enabled?

questions.distractor_summary: Soft delete, versioning, and anonymous access do not add encryption.

questions.subdomain: Configure Azure Files and Azure Blob Storage
questions.question: A container must allow anonymous read access to its blobs for a public website, but listing the container must not be allowed. Which access level should be set?

questions.subdomain: Configure Azure Files and Azure Blob Storage

An ordered, durable log of changes to blobs and their metadata
A list of all users who signed in

questions.subdomain: Configure Azure Files and Azure Blob Storage

An immediate deployment in complete mode

questions.domain: 3. Deploy and manage Azure compute resources

Incremental deletes resources, while complete keeps them
Complete mode only deploys storage accounts

questions.domain: 3. Deploy and manage Azure compute resources

questions.domain: 3. Deploy and manage Azure compute resources

Place it in an availability set only within one rack
Use the archive storage tier for the OS disk

questions.domain: 3. Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
questions.question: What is the purpose of fault domains in an availability set?

Spreading VMs across separate racks with independent power and network to limit the impact of hardware failures

questions.question: What is the purpose of update domains in an availability set?
options: Grouping VMs so that only one group is rebooted at a time during planned maintenance
questions.correct_rationale: Update domains make sure not all VMs reboot at once during maintenance.
questions.distractor_summary: Fault domains separate hardware, and scaling and backup are other features.

questions.domain: 3. Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
questions.question: A VM needs more CPU and memory. What should be done?
options: Resize the VM to a larger size, which may require a restart
Change the OS disk type to Standard HDD
questions.correct_rationale: Resizing changes the VM size and its CPU and memory.
questions.distractor_summary: Disks and network interfaces do not add CPU or memory.

questions.domain: 3. Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
questions.question: A VM cannot be resized to a specific size in the portal because it is not listed. What is a likely reason?

The size is not available on the hardware cluster hosting the VM, so the VM must be deallocated first, or the size is not offered in the region
The VM is in a resource group with a budget
The VM uses a managed identity
questions.correct_rationale: Some sizes require deallocation to move to other hardware, and availability varies by region.
questions.distractor_summary: Tags, budgets, and managed identities do not affect resize options.

questions.domain: 3. Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
questions.question: Which disk type offers the highest performance for latency-sensitive production workloads such as databases?
options: Ultra Disk or Premium SSD v2
questions.correct_rationale: Ultra Disk and Premium SSD v2 provide very high IOPS and low latency.
questions.distractor_summary: Standard disks offer lower performance, and archive storage is not a disk.

questions.domain: 3. Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
questions.question: Data on a VM's data disk must be encrypted using keys the company controls. What should be configured?

Server-side encryption with customer-managed keys through a disk encryption set
questions.correct_rationale: Disk encryption sets link managed disks to customer-managed keys in Key Vault.

questions.domain: 3. Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
questions.question: What does encryption at host do for a VM?
options: Encrypts network traffic to the internet
Encrypts the VM's public IP address
Encrypts data on the VM host, including temporary disks and disk caches, so data is encrypted end to end into storage
questions.correct_rationale: Encryption at host covers temp disks and caches in addition to managed disk encryption.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not encrypt internet traffic or IP addresses, and archive is a blob tier.

questions.domain: 3. Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
questions.question: An administrator needs to move a VM to another resource group in the same subscription. What happens?

The VM and its dependent resources can be moved, and the resource IDs change
Moves are not supported for VMs
questions.correct_rationale: Moving changes the resource group and resource IDs but not the region.
questions.distractor_summary: Recreation is unnecessary, the region stays the same, and VMs can be moved.

questions.domain: 3. Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
questions.question: A company must move a VM to another Azure region. Which service helps with this?
options: Azure Resource Mover, or Azure Site Recovery for replication and failover
questions.correct_rationale: Cross-region moves use Resource Mover or Site Recovery, since resource group moves do not change regions.
questions.distractor_summary: Resource group moves stay in the same region, AzCopy copies data rather than VMs, and locks block changes.

questions.domain: 3. Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
questions.question: Which feature lets you connect securely to VMs over RDP or SSH from the Azure portal without public IP addresses on the VMs?
questions.correct_rationale: Bastion provides browser-based RDP and SSH through a managed host in the virtual network.
questions.distractor_summary: DNS, Front Door, and File Sync do not provide VM access.

questions.domain: 3. Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
questions.question: A VM scale set should add instances when average CPU exceeds 70 percent and remove them below 30 percent. What should be configured?

Autoscale rules on the scale set based on CPU metrics

questions.distractor_summary: Locks, resizing, and availability sets do not scale based on load.

questions.domain: 3. Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
questions.question: Which scale set orchestration mode lets you mix VM sizes and manage individual VMs with standard VM APIs?
questions.correct_rationale: Flexible orchestration supports varied VM types and standard VM operations.
questions.distractor_summary: Uniform uses identical instances, and classic or manual are not scale set modes.

questions.domain: 3. Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
questions.question: A VM must run a script to install software after it is deployed. What is the best way to automate this?

Add a data disk with the software already copied
Use the Custom Script Extension or cloud-init for Linux

questions.domain: 3. Deploy and manage Azure compute resources

questions.question: A team wants to run a container image quickly for a batch task with no cluster to manage. What should they use?

Enable the registry admin user and paste the password
Copy the image to Blob Storage

questions.domain: 3. Deploy and manage Azure compute resources

questions.question: What is a container group in Azure Container Instances?

questions.domain: 3. Deploy and manage Azure compute resources

questions.domain: 3. Deploy and manage Azure compute resources

questions.domain: 3. Deploy and manage Azure compute resources

A CPU autoscale rule on a VM scale set

questions.domain: 3. Deploy and manage Azure compute resources

questions.domain: 3. Deploy and manage Azure compute resources

Virtual network integration for the app
A public IP on the database

questions.domain: 3. Deploy and manage Azure compute resources

questions.subdomain: Configure Azure Files and Azure Blob Storage
questions.question: Which Azure Files tier uses SSD storage for IO-intensive workloads?

questions.distractor_summary: Transaction optimized, hot, and cool are standard HDD-based tiers.

questions.domain: 3. Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
questions.question: A VM's OS disk must be backed up before a risky change so it can be restored quickly. What is a simple option?

Take a snapshot of the managed disk

questions.domain: 3. Deploy and manage Azure compute resources

It is moved to the OS disk

Public IPs always bill as compute
The VM has a tag that forces billing

The Redeploy operation for the VM

questions.domain: 3. Deploy and manage Azure compute resources

An Azure Files share as a volume

questions.question: Which command builds a container image in the cloud and pushes it to Azure Container Registry?

questions.distractor_summary: The other commands create VMs, storage accounts, or virtual networks.

questions.domain: 3. Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
questions.subdomain: Create and configure Azure App Service
questions.question: A web app should send 10 percent of production traffic to a staging slot to test a new version. What should be configured?

Traffic routing percentage for the deployment slot

questions.question: Which setting in App Service keeps a slot-specific value from moving during a swap?

questions.domain: 3. Deploy and manage Azure compute resources

C must have a public IP
A and C must be in the same subnet

Assign a public IP to the spoke

A public IP on each VM
A user-defined route table with a 0.0.0.0/0 route to the appliance's private IP, associated with the subnet

questions.subdomain: Configure and manage virtual networks in Azure

questions.subdomain: Configure and manage virtual networks in Azure

A DNS alias record without an IP

questions.subdomain: Configure and manage virtual networks in Azure

questions.subdomain: Configure and manage virtual networks in Azure

questions.subdomain: Configure and manage virtual networks in Azure
questions.question: Which route next-hop type sends traffic to a firewall or other appliance by its IP address?

options: A user-defined route to the office
A network security group inbound rule allowing TCP 3389 from the office range, with other inbound traffic denied by default
questions.correct_rationale: NSG rules filter traffic by source, port, and protocol.
questions.distractor_summary: Routes do not filter, NAT gateways handle outbound traffic, and DNS does not restrict access.

questions.subdomain: Configure secure access to virtual networks
questions.question: How are NSG rules evaluated?
options: In priority order from the lowest number to the highest, stopping at the first match
All rules are evaluated and the most permissive wins
questions.correct_rationale: Lower numbers have higher priority, and processing stops at the first match.
questions.distractor_summary: The other descriptions do not match NSG behavior.

questions.subdomain: Configure secure access to virtual networks
questions.question: An NSG is associated with both a subnet and a VM's network interface. Inbound traffic is allowed at the subnet but denied at the NIC. What happens?
options: The traffic is allowed, because the subnet NSG wins
The traffic is denied, because inbound traffic must be allowed by both NSGs
The traffic is allowed, because the most permissive rule wins
The NIC NSG is ignored when a subnet NSG exists
questions.correct_rationale: Inbound traffic is checked by the subnet NSG and then the NIC NSG, and both must allow it.
questions.distractor_summary: Neither NSG overrides the other, and NIC NSGs are not ignored.

questions.subdomain: Configure secure access to virtual networks
questions.question: What is an application security group?
options: A way to group VMs by function so NSG rules can reference the group instead of IP addresses
A firewall service for web apps
A group of users with access to apps
questions.correct_rationale: ASGs simplify NSG rules by using logical groups of network interfaces.
questions.distractor_summary: ASGs are not WAFs, user groups, or backend pools.

questions.subdomain: Configure secure access to virtual networks
questions.question: Administrators want to connect to VMs without public IPs or open RDP ports to the internet. What should be deployed?
options: A public IP on each VM
A point-to-site VPN for every VM
Azure Bastion in the virtual network
questions.correct_rationale: Bastion provides secure RDP and SSH from the portal over TLS.
questions.distractor_summary: Public IPs expose VMs, NAT gateways are outbound, and per-VM VPNs are not needed.

questions.subdomain: Configure secure access to virtual networks
questions.question: A subnet must access a storage account over the Azure backbone, and the storage firewall must allow only that subnet, but the account can keep its public endpoint. What should be configured?
options: A private endpoint with a private DNS zone
A public IP on the subnet
A service endpoint for Microsoft.Storage on the subnet and a virtual network rule on the storage account
An NSG deny rule for storage
questions.correct_rationale: Service endpoints extend the subnet identity to the service so the firewall can allow it.
questions.distractor_summary: Private endpoints assign a private IP, which goes beyond this requirement, and public IPs or deny rules do not provide this access.

questions.subdomain: Configure secure access to virtual networks
questions.question: Which tool shows the effective security rules applied to a VM's network interface?
options: Effective security rules in Network Watcher or the NIC blade
questions.correct_rationale: Effective security rules combine all NSG rules that apply to the NIC.
questions.distractor_summary: Advisor cost, the activity log, and Resource Graph do not compute effective rules.

questions.subdomain: Configure secure access to virtual networks
questions.question: Azure services such as a load balancer health probe must be allowed through an NSG without hard-coding IPs. What should be used in the rule?
options: A specific public IP range copied from a website
An application security group of all VMs
questions.correct_rationale: Service tags represent Azure service IP ranges that Microsoft maintains.
questions.distractor_summary: Copied ranges go stale, ASGs group your VMs, and Internet is too broad.

questions.subdomain: Configure name resolution and load balancing
questions.question: VMs in several virtual networks must resolve each other's names in a private domain. What should be configured?
options: An Azure private DNS zone linked to each virtual network, with auto-registration where needed
A host file on each VM
questions.correct_rationale: Private DNS zones provide name resolution across linked virtual networks.
questions.distractor_summary: Public zones expose names, host files do not scale, and NAT gateways do not resolve names.

questions.subdomain: Configure name resolution and load balancing
questions.question: What does auto-registration in an Azure private DNS zone do?
options: It registers the domain with a public registrar
It deletes unused DNS records weekly
It adds a public IP to each VM
It automatically creates DNS records for VMs in the linked virtual network
questions.correct_rationale: Auto-registration creates and removes records as VMs are created and deleted.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not register public domains, delete records on a schedule, or add IPs.

questions.subdomain: Configure name resolution and load balancing
questions.question: A web app on VMs needs layer 7 routing based on URL paths, with a web application firewall. Which service fits?
questions.correct_rationale: Application Gateway is a layer 7 load balancer with path-based routing and WAF.
questions.distractor_summary: Load Balancer is layer 4, NAT gateways handle outbound traffic, and DNS does not load balance requests.

questions.subdomain: Configure name resolution and load balancing
questions.question: Which Azure load balancing service operates at layer 4 and distributes TCP and UDP traffic?
questions.correct_rationale: Azure Load Balancer distributes traffic at the transport layer.
questions.distractor_summary: Application Gateway and Front Door are layer 7, and Traffic Manager uses DNS.

questions.subdomain: Configure name resolution and load balancing
questions.question: An internal load balancer is set up, but VMs in the backend pool get no traffic. The health probe shows them as unhealthy. What should be checked?
options: That the VMs have public IP addresses
That the probe port and path match a listening service and that NSGs allow traffic from the AzureLoadBalancer service tag
That the load balancer has a DNS zone
That the VMs are in the archive tier
questions.correct_rationale: Probes must reach a listening port, and NSGs must allow probe traffic.
questions.distractor_summary: Internal load balancers do not need public IPs, DNS zones are not required, and VMs have no archive tier.

questions.subdomain: Configure name resolution and load balancing
questions.question: Which Azure Load Balancer SKU should be used for new deployments, with zone redundancy and an SLA?
questions.correct_rationale: Standard is the supported SKU, and Basic Load Balancer has been retired.
questions.distractor_summary: Basic is retired, and Classic and Free are not load balancer SKUs.

questions.subdomain: Configure name resolution and load balancing
questions.question: Users must be routed by DNS to the closest healthy regional endpoint of an application. Which service fits?
options: Azure Traffic Manager with performance routing
questions.correct_rationale: Traffic Manager uses DNS to direct users to endpoints by latency, priority, or other methods.
questions.distractor_summary: Load Balancer works within a region, and NAT gateways and NSGs do not route users.

questions.subdomain: Configure name resolution and load balancing
questions.question: What is a load balancing rule in Azure Load Balancer?
options: A DNS record for the load balancer
A mapping of a front-end IP and port to backend pool instances and port, with a health probe
questions.correct_rationale: Load balancing rules define how incoming traffic is distributed to the backend pool.
questions.distractor_summary: DNS records, routes, and NSG rules are separate configurations.

questions.subdomain: Configure name resolution and load balancing
questions.question: VMs behind a Standard internal load balancer lose outbound internet access. What is the recommended way to provide it?
options: Remove the VMs from the backend pool
Associate a NAT gateway with the subnet
questions.correct_rationale: Standard internal load balancers do not provide outbound access, and NAT gateway is the recommended outbound method.
questions.distractor_summary: Basic is retired, removing VMs breaks load balancing, and DNS does not provide outbound access.

questions.subdomain: Configure name resolution and load balancing
questions.question: Which tool can test whether a VM can connect to a specific IP and port, and show where the traffic is blocked?
options: Network Watcher connection troubleshoot or IP flow verify
questions.correct_rationale: Network Watcher diagnostic tools test connectivity and identify the blocking rule or route.
questions.distractor_summary: Advisor, cost analysis, and Policy do not test connectivity.

questions.subdomain: Configure and manage virtual networks in Azure
questions.question: A virtual network needs more address space for new subnets. What can be done without recreating it?
options: Delete all subnets and recreate them
Add an additional address range to the virtual network, updating peerings if required
Convert the subnets to public subnets
questions.correct_rationale: Address ranges can be added to existing VNets, and peered networks can be synced.
questions.distractor_summary: Recreating subnets causes outages, VNets cannot change regions, and Azure has no public subnet type.

questions.subdomain: Configure and manage virtual networks in Azure
questions.question: Which subnet must be named exactly for a VPN gateway to be deployed?
questions.correct_rationale: VPN and ExpressRoute gateways must be deployed into a subnet named GatewaySubnet.
questions.distractor_summary: AzureBastionSubnet is for Bastion, and the other names are not required.

questions.subdomain: Configure and manage virtual networks in Azure
questions.question: A hub-and-spoke network must route spoke-to-spoke traffic through a firewall in the hub. What is required?
options: A public IP on every VM
User-defined routes in each spoke pointing to the firewall, and peerings that allow forwarded traffic
questions.correct_rationale: Spokes need routes to the firewall, and hub peerings must allow forwarded traffic.
questions.distractor_summary: Direct peering bypasses the firewall, public IPs are unrelated, and DNS does not route traffic.

questions.subdomain: Configure and manage virtual networks in Azure
questions.question: Which type of route takes priority when a user-defined route and a system route have the same prefix?
options: BGP routes always win over both
questions.correct_rationale: For identical prefixes, user-defined routes win over BGP and system routes.
questions.distractor_summary: System routes, creation order, and BGP do not win over a UDR with the same prefix.

questions.subdomain: Configure secure access to virtual networks
questions.question: An NSG must deny all outbound traffic to the internet from a subnet but allow traffic within the virtual network. What should be added?
options: An inbound deny rule for the VirtualNetwork tag
An outbound deny rule with the Internet service tag as destination, at a higher priority than any allow rule for it
A route to the internet next hop
questions.correct_rationale: The Internet tag matches public addresses, so denying it blocks internet traffic while VNet traffic stays allowed.
questions.distractor_summary: An inbound VNet deny blocks internal traffic, NAT gateways enable outbound traffic, and an internet route allows it.

questions.subdomain: Configure secure access to virtual networks
questions.question: Which default NSG rule allows traffic between resources in the same virtual network?
questions.correct_rationale: Default rules include AllowVnetInBound and AllowVnetOutBound with priority 65000.
questions.distractor_summary: DenyAllInBound blocks, and the other rules cover internet or load balancer traffic.

questions.subdomain: Configure secure access to virtual networks
questions.question: A company wants central control of outbound filtering with FQDN rules for many virtual networks. What should be used?
options: Azure Firewall in a hub VNet, with routes from spokes to the firewall
An NSG in each subnet with FQDN rules
A NAT gateway with FQDN filtering
questions.correct_rationale: Azure Firewall supports application rules with FQDNs and central management.
questions.distractor_summary: NSGs do not support FQDN rules, NAT gateways do not filter, and DNS zones do not filter traffic.

questions.subdomain: Configure name resolution and load balancing
questions.question: A company hosts its public domain in Azure DNS. The domain registrar must point to Azure. What should be done?
options: Add an A record at the registrar for every VM
Update the domain's name server records at the registrar to the Azure DNS name servers for the zone
questions.correct_rationale: Delegation means setting the registrar's NS records to the zone's Azure name servers.
questions.distractor_summary: Private zones are internal, A records at the registrar do not delegate, and NAT gateways are unrelated.

questions.subdomain: Configure name resolution and load balancing
questions.question: Which DNS record type maps a name to another name?
questions.correct_rationale: A CNAME record aliases one name to another.
questions.distractor_summary: A maps to IPv4 addresses, MX defines mail servers, and TXT holds text.

questions.subdomain: Configure name resolution and load balancing
questions.question: A VM in an Azure VNet must resolve names hosted on an on-premises DNS server. What should be configured?
options: A public DNS zone with the on-premises names
An NSG rule allowing port 53 only
A Private DNS Resolver outbound endpoint with a forwarding ruleset, or custom DNS servers in the VNet that forward to on premises
questions.correct_rationale: Forwarding is needed to send queries for on-premises zones to on-premises DNS.
questions.distractor_summary: Public zones expose names, an NSG rule alone does not forward, and load balancers do not resolve DNS.

questions.question: Administrators want an email when a VM's available memory drops below a threshold. What should be configured?
options: An Azure Monitor metric alert rule with an action group
questions.correct_rationale: Metric alerts evaluate conditions and notify through action groups.
questions.distractor_summary: Policy, budgets, and locks do not monitor performance.

questions.question: What is a Log Analytics workspace?
options: A data store where Azure Monitor log data is collected and queried with KQL
A storage account for VM disks
questions.correct_rationale: Workspaces store log data for queries and alerts.
questions.distractor_summary: It is not a disk store, management group, or network.

questions.question: Guest OS performance counters and event logs must be collected from VMs into a workspace. What should be used?
options: The Azure Monitor Agent with a data collection rule
questions.correct_rationale: Data collection rules tell the Azure Monitor Agent which data to send.
questions.distractor_summary: The activity log covers control plane events, Advisor recommends, and lifecycle rules manage blobs.

questions.question: What does the Azure activity log record?
options: Subscription-level events such as resource creation, changes, and deletion
questions.correct_rationale: The activity log shows control plane operations and who performed them.
questions.distractor_summary: Guest logs, traces, and packets come from other sources.

questions.question: An alert fires too often for brief CPU spikes. How can the noise be reduced while still catching sustained problems?
options: Increase the evaluation window and aggregation period, or use dynamic thresholds
questions.correct_rationale: Longer windows and dynamic thresholds ignore short spikes.
questions.distractor_summary: Deleting removes monitoring, lowering thresholds adds noise, and more action groups add notifications.

questions.question: A team wants to visualize VM performance and dependencies between processes and other servers. What should they enable?
questions.correct_rationale: VM insights shows performance charts and dependency maps.
questions.distractor_summary: Cost analysis, guest configuration, and Bastion do not map dependencies.

questions.question: Which Network Watcher feature captures packets to and from a VM for analysis?
questions.correct_rationale: Packet capture records traffic for troubleshooting.
questions.distractor_summary: IP flow verify checks rules, next hop checks routing, and topology shows the network layout.

questions.question: Which Network Watcher tool tells you the next-hop type and route table used for traffic from a VM to a destination?
questions.correct_rationale: Next hop shows how traffic will be routed and which route applies.
questions.distractor_summary: Packet capture records traffic, VPN troubleshoot diagnoses gateways, and Connection monitor tracks reachability over time.

questions.question: Network traffic metadata for a virtual network must be logged and analyzed for security. Which feature should be used for new deployments?
options: NSG flow logs only, created on new NSGs
Virtual network flow logs with traffic analytics
questions.correct_rationale: Virtual network flow logs replace NSG flow logs for new deployments and work with traffic analytics.
questions.distractor_summary: New NSG flow logs are being phased out, permanent packet capture is impractical, and the activity log does not record traffic.

questions.question: Which Azure Monitor alert type is triggered by a query over log data?
questions.correct_rationale: Log search alerts run KQL queries on a schedule and fire on results.
questions.distractor_summary: Metric and activity log alerts use other signals, and budget alerts are for costs.

questions.question: A team wants to be notified when someone deletes a resource group. What should they configure?
options: An activity log alert for the delete resource group operation
questions.correct_rationale: Activity log alerts trigger on control plane events such as deletions.
questions.distractor_summary: CPU alerts, lifecycle policies, and NSGs do not track deletions.

questions.question: What does Azure Monitor's alert processing rule do?
options: It changes alert behavior, for example suppressing notifications during planned maintenance
questions.correct_rationale: Alert processing rules add or suppress action groups on fired alerts.
questions.distractor_summary: They do not create metrics, delete logs, or assign roles.

questions.question: Which tool should be used to query logs from several VMs for failed sign-in events?
options: Log Analytics with a KQL query
questions.correct_rationale: Log Analytics runs KQL queries across collected logs.
questions.distractor_summary: Storage Explorer, Resource Mover, and the calculator do not query logs.

questions.question: Azure VMs must be backed up daily with 30-day retention. What should be configured?
options: A Recovery Services vault with a VM backup policy
questions.correct_rationale: Azure Backup uses a vault and a policy that sets schedule and retention.
questions.distractor_summary: Lifecycle policies manage blobs, locks block changes, and availability sets do not back up.

questions.question: Which vault type is used for Azure Backup of Azure Disks, blobs, and PostgreSQL servers using newer backup features?
questions.correct_rationale: Backup vaults support newer workloads such as Azure Disk Backup and blob backup.
questions.distractor_summary: Recovery Services vaults support many workloads but not all newer ones, and Key Vault and storage accounts are not backup vaults.

questions.question: Backups must still be recoverable even if a malicious administrator tries to delete them. What should be enabled?
options: A ReadOnly lock on the VMs
Soft delete and immutability on the vault, with multi-user authorization for critical operations
Public network access to the vault
questions.correct_rationale: Soft delete keeps deleted backups, immutability blocks reductions, and MUA requires a second approval.
questions.distractor_summary: VM locks do not protect backups, shorter retention reduces protection, and public access adds risk.

questions.question: A single file was deleted from a backed-up VM. How can it be recovered without restoring the whole VM?
options: Restore the entire VM to a new resource group
Use file recovery from the VM's recovery point by mounting it and copying the file
questions.correct_rationale: File-level recovery mounts a recovery point and lets you copy individual files.
questions.distractor_summary: Full restores are heavier, and File Sync and archive rehydration are unrelated.

questions.question: What does Azure Site Recovery provide?
options: Replication of VMs to a secondary region and orchestrated failover and failback for disaster recovery
questions.correct_rationale: Site Recovery replicates workloads and runs failover plans.
questions.distractor_summary: It is not file backup, cost estimation, or DNS.

questions.question: The company wants to test disaster recovery without affecting production replication. What should be run in Site Recovery?
options: A test failover into an isolated virtual network
questions.correct_rationale: Test failover creates VMs in an isolated network so production is unaffected.
questions.distractor_summary: Planned failover moves production, and deleting or disabling replication stops protection.

questions.question: What is a recovery plan in Azure Site Recovery?
options: An ordered set of machines and steps, including scripts and manual actions, for failover
questions.correct_rationale: Recovery plans group machines and orchestrate failover order.
questions.distractor_summary: Retention schedules, costs, and security rules are other concepts.

questions.question: Backup reports must show backup job success and storage use across many vaults. What should be configured?
options: Diagnostic settings on the vaults sending data to a Log Analytics workspace, and Backup reports
questions.correct_rationale: Backup reports use vault diagnostics data in Log Analytics.
questions.distractor_summary: Budgets track spending, vaults do not use NSGs, and lifecycle policies manage blobs.

questions.question: Backup jobs must be monitored, and alerts sent when a backup fails. What should be used?
options: Azure Monitor alerts for Azure Backup, or the Backup center
questions.correct_rationale: Azure Backup integrates with Azure Monitor for built-in alerts and the Backup center for monitoring.
questions.distractor_summary: DNS, Bastion, and Resource Graph do not alert on backup failures.

questions.question: Which redundancy setting for a Recovery Services vault copies backup data to a paired region?
questions.correct_rationale: GRS replicates backup data to a secondary region for regional resilience.
questions.distractor_summary: LRS and ZRS stay in one region, and Premium SSD is a disk type.

questions.question: VM backups must be restorable to another region if the primary region is unavailable. What should be enabled?
options: Cross Region Restore on a GRS vault
questions.correct_rationale: Cross Region Restore lets you restore backups in the secondary region.
questions.distractor_summary: Soft delete protects deletions, LRS stays local, and locks do not enable restores.

questions.question: When must the backup storage redundancy of a Recovery Services vault be chosen?
options: At any time, even after backups exist
Before any items are protected in the vault
questions.correct_rationale: Storage redundancy must be set before protecting items.
questions.distractor_summary: It cannot be changed freely after backups exist, and it can be configured.

questions.question: A VM backup must capture application-consistent snapshots of a Windows VM running SQL Server. What does Azure Backup use?
options: The Volume Shadow Copy Service (VSS) through the backup extension
questions.correct_rationale: Azure Backup uses VSS on Windows VMs to create application-consistent recovery points.
questions.distractor_summary: Crash-consistent copies do not coordinate with apps, and manual copies and blob versioning are not VM backups.
